Article 3

a. Neglected children are children aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poor/unable, one or both parents/guardian sick or deceased, family not harmonious), cannot have their basic needs properly met, whether physically, spiritually or socially.

b. Children who are victims of gender-based violence or mistreatment are children aged 0-18 years who are threatened physically and non-physically due to violence, are mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly met, whether physically, spiritually or socially.

c. Delinquent children are children aged 0-18 years who behave in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their families and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. Street children are children aged 0-18 years who spend most of their time seeking livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. Children with disabilities are children aged 0-18 years who have physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. Women vulnerable to socio-economic conditions are adult women aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who do not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. Women who are victims of gender-based violence and/or mistreatment are women aged 18-59 years who are threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to violence, are mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 18

(1) Every child has the right to receive social protection and social welfare administration from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.

(2) Every child has the right to receive social protection and social welfare administration to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.

(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of child welfare standards and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.

(4) Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and social mental.

Article 7

Social protection for women and children aims to:

a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children c. increase the level of welfare, quality, and continuity of life. d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence. e. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.
f. increase awareness, ability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, ability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and community.

Article 39

(1) Every person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as regulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

(2) Every person who employs children under the working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as regulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No. 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

Article 19

(1) Every person is prohibited from neglecting, committing violence and/or exploitation against children.

(2) Every person is prohibited from employing children below working age as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 2

The scope of social protection includes: women and children bearing social problems.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 5

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Social protection for women and children aims to:

a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children c. increase the level of welfare, quality, and continuity of life. d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence. e. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.

Article 3

a. Neglected children are children aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poor/unable, one or both parents/guardian sick or deceased, family not harmonious), cannot have their basic needs properly met, whether physically, spiritually or socially.

b. Children who are victims of gender-based violence or mistreatment are children aged 0-18 years who are threatened physically and non-physically due to violence, are mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly met, whether physically, spiritually or socially.

c. Delinquent children are children aged 0-18 years who behave in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their families and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. Street children are children aged 0-18 years who spend most of their time seeking livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. Children with disabilities are children aged 0-18 years who have physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. Women vulnerable to socio-economic conditions are adult women aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who do not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. Women who are victims of gender-based violence and/or mistreatment are women aged 18-59 years who are threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to violence, are mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 5

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

NUMBER 2 OF 2012

CONCERNING

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

II. ELUCIDATION ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 15

Every woman is obliged to maintain her dignity and that of her family as well as her nature as a woman by taking into account her function and role in family and/or community life according to her ability.

Article 35

(1) The regional government shall conduct supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children in accordance with its duties, functions, and authorities.

(2) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted based on the principles of transparency and accountability.

Part One

Guidance

Article 42

All provisions relating to social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children that existed before the enactment of this Regional Regulation, shall remain in effect insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Part Two

Social Protection and Social Welfare Administration for Women

Article 36

(1) Functional supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children shall be carried out by functional supervisory officials.

(2) Technical operational supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be conducted by SKPD/UKPD.

(3) Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 18

(1) Every child has the right to receive social protection and social welfare administration from parents, family, community, and regional government to grow and develop properly.

(2) Every child has the right to receive social protection and social welfare administration to develop their abilities and social life in accordance with the culture and personality of the nation to become a good and useful member of society.

(3) Every child has the right to obtain maintenance of child welfare standards and protection from environments that endanger and/or hinder their growth and development properly.

(4) Every child has the right to receive first aid, assistance and protection in dangerous situations. every child has the right to receive protection from parents against all forms of physical and mental violence, neglect, maltreatment, exploitation and sexual abuse, as well as the right to care, religious guidance, and social mental.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 5

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Article 36

(1) Functional supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children shall be carried out by functional supervisory officials.

(2) Technical operational supervision over social protection and implementation of social welfare for women and children organized by social organizations and the community shall be conducted by SKPD/UKPD.

(3) Further provisions regarding the implementation of supervision shall be regulated by Regent Regulation in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

Article 39

(1) Every person who neglects, commits acts of violence and/or exploitation against children as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (1) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as regulated in Article 77 letter b, Article 80, Article 81, Article 82, and Article 88 of Law No. 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

(2) Every person who employs children under the working age as referred to in Article 19 paragraph (2) shall be subject to criminal sanctions as regulated in Article 185 paragraph (1) of Law No. 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 5

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

Article 5

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

CONCERNING

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 5

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

CONCERNING

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

CONCERNING

SOCIAL PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

The targets of social welfare development regulated in this Regional Regulation are directed toward Women and Children. Especially programs for improving the quality of life and protection of women and children. This is in accordance with the purpose and function of a Regional Regulation to regulate certain matters in accordance with the conditions and needs of a region.

This Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children aims to provide a legal basis for Social Protection efforts for Women and Children as well as provide a study within the philosophical, sociological and juridical framework on the need for a Regional Regulation that becomes the legal foundation for addressing social problems in Wonosobo Regency especially related to Women and Children.

Substantively, in efforts to overcome problems of Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, it is necessary to formulate a Regional Regulation on Social Protection for Women and Children which in essence is an action that is rooted or has a strong foundation, namely in good governance, and should be formulated with proper principles.

Regulation in the field of Social Protection for Women and Children must take into account environmental and social aspects, so that the social condition of society is controlled. Regulation of Social Protection for Women and Children through Regional Regulations can be viewed as a solution as well as an effort to prevent negative impacts that potentially harm the interests of the community.

The absence of a specific Regional Regulation regulating Social Protection for Women and Children in Wonosobo Regency, makes the urgency of this Regional Regulation indeed needed as a legal umbrella for the creation of legal certainty in matters of Social Protection for Women and Children, which is an obligation of the Regional Government especially the Wonosobo Regional Government to provide Social Protection for Women and Children of Wonosobo Regency.

Article 7

Social protection for women and children aims to:

a. eliminate all forms of violence against women and children b. protect, provide a sense of security for women and children c. increase the level of welfare, quality, and continuity of life. d. restore social functions in order to achieve independence. e. increase community social resilience in preventing and handling social welfare problems.
f. increase awareness, ability, concern and social responsibility of the business world in the implementation of social welfare in an institutionalized and sustainable manner.
g. increase awareness, ability, concern and social responsibility of the business world and community.

Article 3

a. Neglected children are children aged 0-18 years who, due to certain reasons (poor/unable, one or both parents/guardian sick or deceased, family not harmonious), cannot have their basic needs properly met, whether physically, spiritually or socially.

b. Children who are victims of gender-based violence or mistreatment are children aged 0-18 years who are threatened physically and non-physically due to violence, are mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs cannot be properly met, whether physically, spiritually or socially.

c. Delinquent children are children aged 0-18 years who behave in deviation from the norms and customs prevailing in society and their environment, thereby harming themselves, their families and others, and will disturb public order, but due to age cannot yet be prosecuted legally.

d. Street children are children aged 0-18 years who spend most of their time seeking livelihood and/or wandering on the streets or in public places.

e. Children with disabilities are children aged 0-18 years who have physical and/or mental abnormalities, which can interfere with or constitute obstacles and barriers for them to carry out activities properly, consisting of persons with physical disabilities, persons with mental disabilities, persons with physical and mental disabilities.

f. Women vulnerable to socio-economic conditions are adult women aged 18-59 years, unmarried or widowed, who do not have sufficient income to meet daily basic needs.

g. Women who are victims of gender-based violence and/or mistreatment are women aged 18-59 years who are threatened physically or non-physically (psychologically) due to violence, are mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment.

h. Trafficking in women and children is the transfer, transportation, mobilization, sending of children and women within a country or abroad illegally and unlawfully, with or without the consent of the person concerned, to be employed exploitatively, especially in the prostitution environment.

Article 5

a. What is meant by "principle of solidarity" is that the implementation of social welfare must be based on social care to help people in need with empathy and compassion.

b. What is meant by "principle of justice" is that the implementation of social welfare must emphasize aspects of equity, non-discrimination and balance between rights and obligations.

c. What is meant by "principle of benefit" is that the implementation of social welfare must provide benefits for improving the quality of life of citizens.

d. What is meant by "principle of integration" is that the implementation of social welfare must integrate various related components so that it can run in a coordinated and synergistic manner.

e. What is meant by "principle of partnership" is that in addressing social welfare issues, partnership is required between the Government and society, with the Government as the responsible party and society as the Government's partner in addressing social welfare issues and improving social welfare.

f. What is meant by "principle of openness" is to provide the widest possible access to society to obtain information related to the implementation of social welfare.

g. What is meant by "principle of accountability" is that every implementation of social welfare must be accountable in accordance with the provisions of statutory regulations.

h. What is meant by "principle of participation" is that every implementation of social welfare must involve all components of society.

i. What is meant by "principle of professionalism" is that every implementation of social welfare to society should be based on professionalism in accordance with their scope of duties and carried out as optimally as possible.

j. What is meant by "principle of sustainability" is that the implementation of social welfare is carried out continuously, so that independence is achieved.

k. What is meant by "principle of non-discrimination" is treatment that does not differentiate based on ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status of children, birth order of children, and physical and mental conditions.

l. What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, socio-cultural, educational and national defense and security (hankamnas) activities, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.
